concerns.message: The attempt resolves on eligibility at landing, and a failed landing is 'attempt-missed' with a cooldown. So if a third party's hit reserves the defender one tick before this attempt lands, the attacker pays the 6 s miss cooldown. If the two hits land on the same tick, the second is 'preempted' at no cost. decisions.md says only a real miss should cost the cooldown ('the attacker didn't miss'). A defender who is reserved (or starts respawning) during the windup did not escape.
concerns.consequence: Two identical situations one tick apart get opposite penalties, and the scripted and property tests will lock in the unfair version. Fixing it later means changing tests and events in encounters-online. Recommendation: when the defender becomes reserved or ineligible for a reason other than moving, cancel or preempt the attempt at that tick with no cooldown. Keep 'missed' for range, cone and line of sight only.

concerns.message: End reports are described only 'for a fight that ran'. The ledger can resolve a duel before the fight starts: during the 3 to 10 s transition, an explicit quit makes the ledger forfeit that player at once (the recordResult forfeit path in objectives/duels.ts), and a server fault can also end the duel early. If the encounter state refuses end reports during the transition, it keeps counting down. At 10 s it emits its own readiness forfeit, or a cancel, which can contradict the ledger's win, and its end tick is wrong by up to 10 s.
concerns.consequence: The loser's 15 s respawn is timed from the wrong tick, a duel can be ended twice with different outcomes, and the settlement report may reach a duel the encounter still thinks is in transition. Recommendation: accept an end report in both the transition and running phases, and let it stop the readiness timer. Add one scripted test for a quit during the countdown.

concerns.message: Draw and cancel returns ask for two distinct navigable points at least 3 tiles apart and within 6 tiles. Four things are missing. (1) Which 'encounter position' to use when the two players stood at different points. (2) A fallback when no such pair exists: narrow channels, or small synthetic maps in the property test. (3) Reachability: seaValidation only checks that docks and spawn slots are reachable, not every navigable tile, so a point across a thin island strip or in an enclosed pocket passes 'navigable'. (4) What happens when a point is taken by another ship.
concerns.consequence: On a synthetic map the property test either fails or the worker adds an unreviewed fallback. In live play a ship can be put on the far side of land or stuck in an unreachable pocket. Recommendation: search outward (breadth-first) from the encounter tile over navigable tiles within 6 tiles, which guarantees the points are connected by sea. Pick the pair deterministically, and document a fallback (for example, the best pair found, otherwise both at the encounter tile).

concerns.message: The hit area at landing is 'within range and within ±4 headings of the aim locked at the start', but it doesn't say where the cone starts: at the attacker's position at the start of the attempt, or where the attacker is at landing. With a locked aim and a moving start point, the attacker can partly steer the grapple during the windup by sailing sideways.
concerns.consequence: Whichever reading the worker picks becomes documented rules and tests. It sets how easy escape is, which is the fairness core of §6, and changing it later is rework. Settle it in docs/encounters.md: I recommend the positions of both players at landing, since the snapshot holds only current positions.

concerns.message: The encounter state tracks its own copy of each duel's lifecycle (reserved, transition, running, ended, settled). The ledger already tracks the same thing (fighting, choosing, settled), and the caller must keep the two in sync with separate end and settlement reports. The cap rule ('counts until settlement'), refused second end reports, and forfeits inside the encounter state all come from keeping two sources of truth.
concerns.consequence: The two states can drift apart, for example on the quit-in-transition path above, or when the ledger refuses a report the encounter already accepted. That produces cap miscounts or ghost duels that encounters-online must debug over the network. The worker should add a property check that every reservation event is followed by exactly one end and one settlement before release.

concerns.message: sea-compact-fixes runs at the same time and owns the sea, the sailing constants and possibly heading.ts and the slice sea map. Scripted encounter tests that hard-code coordinates or literal ranges on the slice sea will break when that feature changes the map or ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES / SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES.
concerns.consequence: Failures appear at merge and are hard to attribute. Keep scripted geometry tests on small synthetic maps. Slice-sea property tests should sample positions from the map's navigable tiles and docks, and every range should come from the imported constants.

concerns.message: The loser's respawn dock rule doesn't say when the dock is chosen: at settlement, when the loser returns, or at the respawn tick 15 s after the fight ended. It also doesn't say who counts as an 'other active player': players in a duel (shown as a marker), respawning players, disconnected players.
concerns.consequence: Choosing at settlement uses opponent positions up to about 10 s old, so the dock can be camped by the time the loser appears, which undermines the anti-camping reason in decisions.md. Recommendation: choose at the respawn tick, counting only players who are in the world and in ship mode. Document it and test it.

concerns.message: The scope is large for one lane with a two-hour stop rule. It covers two modes, integer geometry, attempts and same-tick resolution, the readiness transition, duel bookkeeping, three return rules, protection, match end, symmetry and seeded property tests with EXERCISED coverage, the content zod schema, docs and two subpath exports.
concerns.consequence: There is a real chance the lane reports 'blocked' after two hours with property or coverage tests failing, or ships with thin return and transition tests. Build the geometry and attempt/resolution core with its tests first, so any partial result is still useful.

simpler_alternative: Keep the encounter state to what only it knows: attempts, cooldowns, protection, the readiness countdown and respawn timers. Take 'in or reserved for a duel' and the unresolved-duel count from the snapshot, which the caller derives from the ledger. Also count hits accepted earlier in the same step, so the four-duel cap holds within one tick. This removes the second duel lifecycle, the separate end-then-settlement reports, the refused second end, and the risk of the two states drifting apart. Return placement (the winner's position, the loser's dock, the two draw points) becomes pure helper functions that the caller runs when the ledger settles the duel, tested on their own. This keeps every rule in the task. It only moves where the duel state lives, and it matches the ledger as the single writer for duel outcomes (§14).
cheap_experiment: Before coding, write a 30-line throwaway script on the compact slice sea. (a) For every navigable tile, check whether a breadth-first search over navigable tiles within 6 tiles finds two tiles at least 3 apart, and whether every navigable tile is reachable by sea from spawn slot 0. (b) Tabulate grapple landings with the ±4 cone and 1 s windup: defender at 1 to 6 tiles, stationary or at full speed with each of the 64 headings, starting from standstill or already at speed (39 sub-units per step, acceleration 3), measuring the cone from the attacker's position at landing. If (a) finds pockets or tiles with no valid pair, the draw rule must switch to a sea-connected search with a fallback. If (b) shows grapples almost never land except on stationary or tail-chased ships, the hit-area rule (cone start, ±4 width) should be settled now rather than after playtests, because the tests will lock it in.
